newsitem.title: USA: Mass Gov't Land Bank sets $80 mln bond sale.
newsitem.headline: Mass Gov't Land Bank sets $80 mln bond sale.

text.p: Massachusetts Government Land Bank said it was planning to sell in the next two weeks about $80 million of mostly taxable bonds to pay for turning former Army base Fort Devens into a commercial center.

Patricia Gannon Simard, managing director with Massachusetts Development Finance Agency, explained on Wednesday that the land bank had been paying for infrastructure and other improvements directly, as it waited for the state legislature to approve the debt sale.
The development agency includes two quasi government agencies, the land bank and the Massachusetts Industrial Finance Agency.

The contract assistance bonds will be sold through PaineWebber, though the rest of the syndicate still is being selected, the official said. About $60 million of the offering will be taxable and around $20 million of tax-exempt bonds.
Fort Devens is about 40 miles northwest of Boston.

Coming sales include one by Suffolk University, which expects to sell about $46 million of tax-exempt, revenue bonds to build a new law school in downtown Boston. That offering, which is slated for around August 19 or 20, would be sold through a syndicate led by State Street Bank.

Eastern Nazarene College in Quincy plans to sell $14 million of taxable and tax-exempt bonds, which will pay a variable rate and be backed by a letter of credit. That sale, which also will be handled by State Street Bank, is slated for around mid-September.
Further, an $11 million sale by Massachusetts Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals likely will occur in mid-August, the official said.

The proceeds from the sale of the tax-exempt revenue bonds, which will pay a variable-rate of interest and be backed by a letter of credit, will be used to improve three different facilities across the state. State Street Bank will lead the syndicate.
